items.headline: September CPI runs hot: 3.7% headline, 2.6% core
items.blurb: US consumer prices rose 0.6% in September, lifting annual inflation to 3.7% from 3.4%, with gasoline driving much of the jump; core also beat forecasts.
items.why_matters: A hotter print keeps a rate hike in play at the Oct 27–28 FOMC — higher-for-longer rates are the main macro headwind for crypto demand.

items.headline: Stocks have their worst day since July; BTC bends but holds ~$81.6k
items.blurb: The S&P 500 fell about 1.1% and the Nasdaq about 1.9% on the CPI print, while bitcoin slipped roughly 2% on the day and is flat on the week, still up about 8% on the month.
items.why_matters: Crypto holding its range while equities sold off is a sign of resilience; a daily close under ~$80k would break the range and flip the 7D view to Bear.

items.headline: BTC ETFs: Tuesday inflow breaks the run, Wednesday tracking red
items.blurb: US spot bitcoin ETFs took in about $176M on Oct 13, led by Fidelity and BlackRock; Oct 14 was tracking an outflow but was not complete at this rebuild. The last five complete sessions are still net negative (about −$598M).
items.why_matters: One green day isn't a trend — demand needs a run of inflows to support a push back toward $86k.

items.headline: Futures deleveraging is slowing, not reversing
items.blurb: CheckOnChain still shows a Deleveraging Sell-Off as of Oct 14, but the seven-day drop in futures OI eased to about 1% against a ~2% price slip; funding stays mildly positive.
items.why_matters: Most forced-selling fuel has been burned off, which helps a floor hold — but nobody is adding leverage yet to drive a rally.

items.headline: RSDH stays SOL-heavy BULL; trail vs BTC widens to 0.11
items.blurb: Investorius RSDH remains SOL95/BTC5/CASH0 under a BULL macro; the fast score eased again to 29. Final× 1.19 vs BTC 1.30 — a week ago it was 1.32 vs 1.33.
items.why_matters: The model is fully invested but SOL's lag in the chop has erased its monthly edge over BTC; a further fade in the fast score is the thing to watch for a de-risk.
